stances.claim: Sensational legislative admissions -- even direct ones from the Discayas and DPWH officials -- cannot by themselves authorize criminal charges, because legislative inquiries are in aid of legislation, with no respondents, accused, or even witnesses, only 'resource persons'; criminal prosecution must come from OMB and DOJ.

Given the damning record produced in legislative hearings and amplified by media, the OMB and DOJ should motu proprio conduct transparent parallel investigations and, at a minimum, open preliminary investigations as evidence surfaces.

DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon is the institutional model -- visiting the deficient projects, going personally to the OMB, and swearing to the evidence -- and the OMB should accept that posture rather than awaiting interminable inquiries.

Republic Act No. 1379 (1955) is a powerful, straightforward, and underused statute: the government need only allege the official's wealth (including that of spouse, ascendants, descendants, relatives, and holders) is not commensurate with lawful earnings, and the burden shifts to the official to prove legal acquisition; failure means forfeiture of the excess to the government.
stances.confidence: asserted, expressly endorsed by quoted compañera Prodigalidad

stances.claim: The lifestyle checks recently ordered by President Marcos will amount to 'idle talk and media extravaganza' unless they result, after due process, in actual RA 1379 forfeitures of ill-gotten wealth -- and the JBC must rush the OMB shortlist so the President can install a new anti-graft czar to deliver speedy justice.

notable_anecdotes: Curlee and Sarah Discaya and several DPWH officials admitting in legislative hearings that billions of pesos ended up in plunderers' pockets, naming honorable members of Congress among the cohorts -- used to dramatize the gap between explosive admissions and absent prosecutions.

DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon personally visiting the deficient flood-control projects, then going to the OMB himself and swearing to the truth and authenticity of the evidence against Bulacan first-district engineering officers and private contractors -- cited as the model an Ombudsman should emulate.

ACCRA managing partner Patricia Prodigalidad's quoted text message endorsing CJ's view and lamenting the government's near-total non-use of RA 1379 -- a peer-confirmation device built into the column.

The 'garish display of expensive watches, cars, real estate in gated villages, condominiums, and branded accessories' as the sensory backdrop of lifestyle checks -- a concrete inventory rather than an abstract phrase.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban answers the vehement reader question -- why can't Curlee and Sarah Discaya's and the DPWH officials' billion-peso admissions in legislative hearings be used by Congress itself to file criminal cases? -- by reciting the doctrine that legislative inquiries are in aid of legislation and only secondarily prosecutorial, with 'resource persons' rather than respondents. He argues that the OMB and DOJ must therefore motu-proprio launch transparent parallel investigations on the public-record evidence already produced, taking DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon's swift filing of non-bailable charges (after personally inspecting projects and swearing to the evidence at the OMB) as the operational template. Citing a text-message exchange with ACCRA managing partner Patricia Prodigalidad, he revives Republic Act No. 1379 (1955) as a powerful but underused forfeiture statute under which the government need only allege that an official's wealth -- including wealth in the names of spouse, ascendants, descendants, relatives, or holders -- is not commensurate with lawful earnings, shifting the burden to the official to prove legal acquisition; if unproven, the excess is forfeited. President Marcos's recently ordered lifestyle checks will amount to 'idle talk and media extravaganza' unless they result, after due process, in actual RA 1379 forfeitures of the garish watches, cars, gated-village houses, condominiums, and branded accessories on display. He closes calling on the OMB to 'show its teeth' and on the JBC to rush its shortlist so the President can install a new anti-graft czar to lead open, transparent, accountable, and credible hearings -- and on all public officials to release their SALNs.
